core.big_idea: God heard Israel's suffering and acted to rescue them.

passages.reading_note: Notice the four actions: heard, remembered, saw, knew.
Focus on God’s call, His knowledge of suffering, His rescue purpose, and His promise to be with Moses.

core.metanarrative_position: Exodus rescue begins: God attends to His oppressed people and calls Moses to bring them out of Egypt.

claims.statement: God heard Israel’s groaning, remembered His covenant, saw the people, and knew.
God told Moses that He had seen the affliction, heard the cry, and knew the suffering of His people.
God announced His purpose to deliver Israel from Egypt and bring them to a good land.
God called Moses to participate in the rescue and promised to be with him.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify repeated seeing, hearing, knowing, and acting words; connect divine compassion to a safe response to suffering.

learning.foundation_objective: Retell that God heard, saw, knew, and acted when Israel suffered.
learning.extension_objective: Explain that God called Moses into the rescue and name a safe way to notice and seek help for suffering today.
know: God heard, remembered, saw, and knew.
God called Moses and promised to be with him.
understand: God’s attention is active compassion, not distant observation.
God often involves people in helping and protecting others.
practise: Pray for someone who is suffering without demanding private details.
Tell a trusted adult when someone may be unsafe.
become: A child who believes suffering matters, prays, notices, and seeks safe help.
success_evidence: The child names the four verbs in Exodus 2.
The child connects Moses’ call to God’s rescue purpose.
The child names a safe adult-help response in a fictional example.

zero_prep_card.objective: Children explain that God heard, saw, knew, and acted when Israel suffered.
zero_prep_card.opening: Show an ear and an eye picture. Ask: What is the difference between noticing a problem and helping?
say: The Israelites were suffering in Egypt.
God heard, remembered, saw, and knew.
God planned rescue and called Moses to help.
God promised Moses, I will be with you.
ask: What four actions are named in Exodus 2?
What did God say He knew?
What job did God give Moses?
Who is a safe adult we can go to when someone needs help?
zero_prep_card.do: Complete the Hear, See, Know, Act picture sequence.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray: God, hear people who suffer. Help us notice, pray, and seek safe help.
materials: Hear, See, Know, Act cards or four drawings

preparation.passage_context: Exodus 1-2 describes Israelite oppression and the growth of Moses. The transition into Exodus 3 explicitly grounds the rescue in God’s covenant memory and compassionate knowledge.
text_observations: Exodus 2:23-25 uses a dense sequence of divine attention verbs.
Exodus 3:7 repeats seeing, hearing, and knowing before announcing deliverance.
God sends Moses and pairs the commission with the promise of His presence.
interpretation_notes: Remembered does not mean God had forgotten; in covenant language it signals action in line with His promise.
Keep Moses as a participant in God’s rescue, not the source of rescue.
Do not promise immediate or spectacular removal from every hardship.
theological_guardrails: Do not imply that unanswered prayer means God did not hear.
Do not ask children to identify suffering, abuse, or danger in their own home.
Do not tell children to confront a dangerous person; direct them to safe adults and established procedures.

likely_questions.question: Why did God wait before rescuing them?
likely_questions.purpose: Acknowledge that the passage does not explain every aspect of timing; it emphasises that God knew and acted according to His covenant purpose.

likely_questions.question: Does God always stop bad things straight away?
likely_questions.purpose: No. We pray, seek help, and trust that suffering matters to God without promising a timetable.

discussion_questions.question: Which four words describe God’s attention in Exodus 2?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Explain why remembered is covenant action, not absent-mindedness.

discussion_questions.question: What did God plan to do?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Identify the movement from Egypt toward the promised land.

discussion_questions.question: Why was Moses part of the story?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Distinguish God’s rescue from Moses’ role.

discussion_questions.question: What is a safe helping response today?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Pray and tell a trusted adult.
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Explain why children should not carry adult danger alone.

activities.title: Hear, See, Know, Act Sequence
materials: Four symbol cards: ear, eye, heart, footprints
steps: Add Act to show rescue purpose.
Add a Moses marker as the person God sent.
activities.learning_link: Turns repeated verbs into a concrete rescue sequence.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Use gestures for ear, eyes, heart, and walking.

activities.title: Notice, Pray, Tell
steps: Choose a trusted adult rather than direct confrontation.
activities.learning_link: Practises safe compassion without inviting disclosure.

closing.prayer_prompt: Pray for people who suffer and for wise, safe helpers.
closing.take_home_line: God heard, saw, knew, and acted to rescue His people.

family.title: Hear, See, Know, Act
family.parent_intro: This study shows that God’s compassion includes attention and action.

flow.instructions: Use the opening prompt to connect the lesson to ordinary family life.
Circle or repeat the words heard, saw, knew, send, and with you.
Use ear, eye, heart, and shoe objects to retell the sequence.
Choose the weekly action, then pray together.

questions: What does God notice in the passage?

interactive.title: Four Compassion Gestures
interactive.instructions: Touch ear, point to eyes, place hand near heart, and make walking fingers to retell the verbs.

family.weekly_action: Choose one person or group to pray for, then name one appropriate adult-led helping action.
family.prayer: God, hear those who suffer. Give wise helpers courage and keep people safe.
family.parent_note: Do not ask a child to disclose danger during the study. Any independent safety disclosure should be handled through safeguarding procedures.

quiz.question: Which word appears in Exodus 2:23-25?
quiz.explanation: The text says God heard the groaning.

quiz.question: Who did God call to go to Pharaoh?
God promised Moses that He would be with him.
What is a safe response when someone may be in danger?
quiz.explanation: Children should seek safe adult help.

puzzle.title: God’s Compassion Sequence
puzzle.instructions: Put the four action words in the lesson order.

printables.title: Hear, See, Know, Act Cards
printables.purpose: Help children remember the compassion and rescue sequence in Exodus 2-3.

accessibility.reading_level: Short concrete sentences suitable for teacher-led reading with ages 4-8.
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Use concrete verbs and define every abstract term through the story.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow pointing, drawing, or one-word responses.
Give one direction at a time.
sensory_notes: Participation must not require loud noise, touch, or public performance.
non_reader_support: Use pictures, objects, or gesture-supported retelling.

do_not_ask: Do not ask children to describe danger or suffering in their own home.
Do not instruct children to confront a dangerous person.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Keep examples fictional. If a child independently discloses possible harm, listen, reassure them they did the right thing by telling, and follow safeguarding procedures.
